summary: All 4 arms in iteration 6 were confirmed exactly as predicted, validating that the Bracket K=1 search strategy generalizes from H100 to A100-SXM hardware. The experiments tested qwen3-14b on A100-SXM across different request rates and demonstrated that TP-selection patterns follow the same rate-dependent transition seen on H100, with the crossover point shifting from ~125 (H100) to ~200 (A100-SXM) consistent with bandwidth differences.
key_points: h-main: At rate=100, TP8/1-instance was selected as winner by all 25 seed combinations (5 search × 5 BLIS seeds) with deterministic evals_to_best=4. Phase 1 scores matched predictions within 0.01% (TP1=0.0804, TP2=0.1055, TP4=0.1275, TP8=0.1308).

h-robustness: TP8 margins over TP4 ranged 3.7–5.2% across BLIS seeds (predicted 2–5%), all well above the 1% selection threshold. Zero variance in winner selection across all 25 combinations confirms deterministic Phase 1 behavior (RP-9).

h-ablation (rate=200): Confirmed exact TP4=TP8 crossover at 0.1345, with evals_to_best=3 (not 4) because TP4 at position 3 clears threshold first. Phase 2 TPE discovered a new global best (0.135440 vs prior 0.134935) via round-robin routing—a 0.38% improvement requiring a table update.

h-control-negative: Flat TPE found global best on all 5 seeds with median evals_to_best=6 (vs Bracket's deterministic 4), but with high variance (range 1–18). Bracket is 33% more efficient at median and critically offers zero variance in convergence time.

Cross-hardware generalization confirmed: A100-SXM follows the same rate-dependent TP transition pattern as H100. Bracket K=1 requires no modification to work correctly across tested hardware platforms and rate regimes.
